Rashi on Gittin 64b:10:1.english: This and that - These two enactments have the same law:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:10:2.english: What [is meant by] "are one"? - [Does it mean] both of them [can] acquire, or both of them cannot acquire?

Rashi on Gittin 64b:11:1.english: Vardan - [he was] from the people of Vardania, a place:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:11:2.english: Merge in an alleyway - so that all the courtyards may carry out into it, and [the residents] may carry in all of them:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:11:3.hebrew: את החבית - שהיין בתוכה לשיתוף, דסתם שיתוף ביין:
Rashi on Gittin 64b:11:3.english: The barrel - in which the wine is [contained] for the shittuf [merging of alleyways], for an unspecified shittuf is [made] with wine:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:12:1.english: What is she doing with him - Behold, she goes free with [puberty] signs:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:13:1.english: Merging of alleyways is by rabbinic law - For by Torah law, it is not forbidden to bring [objects] in and take [them] out except from a private domain to a public domain:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:14:1.hebrew: אשתיק וורדאן - נאלם, שלא השיב תשובה על תירוץ זה:
Rashi on Gittin 64b:14:1.english: Vardaan was silent - He fell silent, [in] that he did not give an answer to this resolution:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:1:1.english: To stringency - Like that [case] of Rabbi Yitzchak:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:4:1.hebrew: היא ואביה - או היא או אביה. היא יש לה יד, דהא גדולה היא, ואביה נמי זכאי לקבלו; ומ"מ יד דידה כדקיימא קיימא, דהא גדולה היא, ואם היתה יתומה, היא מהוה את עצמה והיא מקבלת את גיטה, והשתא נמי לא שנא:
Rashi on Gittin 64b:4:1.english: She and her father - Either she or her father. She has a "hand" [i.e., legal capacity to receive], for she is an adult, and her father is also entitled to receive it; nevertheless, her own "hand" remains intact, for she is an adult, and if she were an orphan, she would be [legally] independent and would receive her bill of divorce, and now too it is no different:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:5:1.hebrew: יד דידה לאו כלום היא - דלגמרי אוקמה רחמנא ברשותיה כל ימי נערות, אלא א"כ ניסת:
Rashi on Gittin 64b:5:1.english: Her hand is nothing - for the Merciful One placed her completely under his [i.e., her father's] authority all the days of [her] maidenhood, unless she is married:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:6:1.hebrew: אינה מתגרשת - דכתיב: "ושלחה מביתו" — מי שמשלחה ואינה חוזרת, יצתה זו שמשלחה וחוזרת. הכי דרשינן לה ביבמות בפרק חרש שנשא (יבמות דף קיג:); הלכך אפילו בקבלת אביה אינה מתגרשת:
Rashi on Gittin 64b:6:1.english: Cannot be divorced - as it is written: "and he sends her away from his house" — [referring to] one whom he sends away and she does not return; excluded is this [girl], whom he sends away and she returns. This is how we expound it in Yevamot, in the chapter Cheresh SheNasa (Yevamot 113b); therefore, even through her father's receipt [of the bill of divorce], she cannot be divorced:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:7:1.hebrew: כל שמשמרת דבר אחר מחמת גיטה - שאם אבדה גיטה, משמרת דבר אחר שאינו דומה לו, וסבורה שהוא גיטה:
Rashi on Gittin 64b:7:1.english: Any [minor] who safeguards something else on account of her bill of divorce - [Meaning] that if she lost her bill of divorce, she safeguards something else that does not resemble it, and thinks that it is her bill of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:8:1.hebrew: הא שוטה בעלמא היא - ואין לך משלחת וחוזרת יותר ממנה, דמדלא קתני "שמשמרת שטר אחר", מכלל דלאו שטר הוא אלא מידי דלא דמי ליה:
Rashi on Gittin 64b:8:1.english: She is merely an imbecile - and there is no [greater example of a woman who is] sent away [in divorce] and returns than her; for since it did not teach "who safeguards another document," it implies that [what she is guarding] is not a document, but rather something that does not resemble it:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:9:1.hebrew: [צרור וזורקו] - קטן שנותנין לו צרור וזורקו, וכשנותנין לו אגוז נוטלו:
Rashi on Gittin 64b:9:1.english: [A pebble and he throws it] - A minor to whom one gives a pebble and he throws it [away], and when one gives him a nut he takes it:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:9:2.hebrew: זוכה לעצמו ואינו זוכה לאחרים - אם זיכה אדם לחברו דבר ע"י אותו קטן, שמסר בידו החפץ ואמר: "זכה בחפץ זה לפלוני", לא זכה; ואם בא הנותן לחזור, חוזר:
Rashi on Gittin 64b:9:2.english: He acquires for himself, and does not acquire for others - If a person transferred [ownership of] something to his fellow through that minor, [in] that he placed the item in his hand and said, "Acquire this item for so-and-so," he [the recipient] has not acquired [it]; and if the giver comes to retract, he may retract:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:9:3.english: An item and he returns it after a while - when they demand it from him:

Rashi on Gittin 64b:9:4.english: He acquires [property] even for others - And [this is] by rabbinic decree:

Tosafot on Gittin 64b:12:1.hebrew: אלא לאו דלא אתיא שתי שערות - וא"ת: מאי שנא שפחה מבנו ובתו הקטנים, דאין מזכה על ידם? ואור"ת, דלרבי יוחנן דאמר בפ"ק דב"מ (דף יב:) גבי מציאה: "לא גדול גדול ממש [כו'], אלא גדול הסמוך על שלחנו של אביו הוא קטן", הוא הדין כאן; אבל שפחה, בשכר טורחה אוכלת. ולשמואל דאמר התם: "קטן קטן ממש", ומפרש טעמא התם: "בשעה שהוא מוצאה מריצה אצל אביו", צריך לומר דמהאי טעמא לכל דבר ידו כיד אביו. ועל חנם דחק לומר ר"ת דשפחה אוכלת בשכרה, דנראה דלא חשבינן יתום ידו כיד בעל הבית בשביל שהוא סמוך על שלחנו, אלא דוקא בבנו; דכל הסמוכין על שלחן בעל הבית, אין מציאתם שלו. ובתו, נראה דאפי' אין סמוכה על שלחן אביה, מציאתה שלו משום איבה, דלמא מסר לה למנוול ומוכה שחין, כדאיתא בפ' נערה (כתובות דף מז.); דטעמא משום איבה שייך אפי' אינה סמוכה על שלחנו, ואף בנערה עד שתיבגר. וצריך ליזהר שלא לזכות ערוב ע"י בנו, אפי' גדול, אם סמוך על שולחנו; דקיי"ל כר' יוחנן לגבי שמואל, דלאו גדול גדול ממש. ואין לתמוה דהכא אמר שפחה שהיא קטנה זוכה בעירוב, ובפ' מי שהוציאוהו (עירובין דף מט:) אמרי' דלשמואל דאמר עירוב משום קנין קטן לא, דהתם דאית ליה בית לקטן קאמר:
Tosafot on Gittin 64b:12:1.english: Rather, is it not [a case] where she did not develop two hairs - And if you ask: What is the difference between a maidservant and one's minor son and daughter, through whom one cannot grant [a share in an eruv]? And Rabbeinu Tam says that according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who says in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (12b) regarding a found object, "'Adult' does not mean literally an adult [etc.], rather an adult who is supported at his father's table is [considered] a minor," the same applies here; whereas a maidservant eats in exchange for her toil. And according to Shmuel, who says there, "'Minor' means literally a minor," and explains the reason there [as being that] "at the time he finds it, he runs it over to his father," one must say that for this reason, for all matters his hand is like his father's hand. However, Rabbeinu Tam forced himself in vain to say that a maidservant eats for her wages, for it appears that we do not consider an orphan's hand to be like the homeowner's hand merely because he is supported at his table, rather specifically [we say this] regarding his son; for [regarding] all [others] who are supported at the homeowner's table, their found objects do not belong to him. And [as for] his daughter, it appears that even if she is not supported at her father's table, her found object belongs to him because of ill-will, lest he give her in marriage to a repulsive or boil-afflicted man, as is stated in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah (Ketubot 47a); for the reason of ill-will applies even if she is not supported at his table, and even [when she is] a na'arah, until she becomes a bogeret. And one must be careful not to grant an eruv through his son, even an adult, if he is supported at his table; for we hold like Rabbi Yoḥanan against Shmuel, that "adult" does not mean literally an adult. And one should not be astonished that here [the Gemara] says a maidservant who is a minor acquires in an eruv, whereas in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehotzi'uhu (Eruvin 49b) we say that according to Shmuel, who says eruv is because of acquisition, a minor does not [acquire], for there it is speaking [of a case] where the minor has a house:

Tosafot on Gittin 64b:13:1.hebrew: שאני שתופי מבואות דרבנן - משמע דרב יהודה ורב חסדא פליגי אי זוכה לאחרים מדאוריתא או לא. ואע"ג דמציאת חרש שוטה וקטן לא הוי גזל אפילו לרבי יוסי אלא מדבריהם, הכא דדעת אחרת מקנה אותם שאני. וא"ת: והא זכיה היא מטעם שליחות, ואין שליחות לקטן מ"אתם גם אתם" (קידושין מא:)? וי"ל: דאין למעט קטן משליחות מקרא דתרומה אלא במילתא דליתיה, כגון תרומה, דליתיה בתרומה דנפשיה; אבל בזכיה, כמו שזוכה לעצמו, זוכה נמי לאחרים. וא"ת: תקשי ליה לרב יהודה הא דאמרי' בריש האיש מקדש (קידושין דף מב.): "איש זוכה ואין קטן זוכה"? וי"ל: דהתם לא מיירי בדעת אחרת מקנה אותו, אלא לאשמועינן דפסח שלו אינו יכול להמנות אחרים עליו, דסלקא דעתין שיוכל להמנות משום דשה לבית אבות דאורייתא, והוי לענין פסח כמו גדול; אי נמי, היא גופה קמ"ל, דשה לבית אבות לאו דאורייתא, ואין לו כח לזכות בו לא לאחרים ולא לעצמו:
Tosafot on Gittin 64b:13:1.english: The merging of alleyways is different, as it is rabbinic - This implies that Rav Yehuda and Rav Ḥisda disagree [as to] whether [a minor] can acquire on behalf of others by Torah law or not. And even though the lost property found by a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor is not [considered] robbery even according to Rabbi Yosei except by rabbinic decree, here, [where] another person's intent transfers ownership to them, it is different. And if you ask: But acquisition [on behalf of another] operates on the principle of agency, and there is no agency for a minor, [as derived] from "you, also you" (Kiddushin 41b)? One can answer: We only exclude a minor from agency [based] on the verse of terumah in a matter in which he is not [eligible], such as terumah, since he is not [eligible to separate] his own terumah; however, regarding acquisition, just as he acquires for himself, he also acquires for others. And if you ask: Let that which we say at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] HaIsh Mekadesh (Kiddushin 42a) be a difficulty for Rav Yehuda: "A man acquires [for others], and a minor does not acquire [for others]"? One can answer: There it is not speaking of [a case where] another person's intent transfers ownership to him; rather, [it comes] to teach us that regarding his [own] Paschal offering, he cannot register others upon it — for it might have entered our mind that he could register [them], because "a lamb for a father's house" is by Torah law, so he would be like an adult with respect to the Paschal offering. Alternatively, it teaches us this very thing: that "a lamb for a father's house" is not by Torah law, and he has no power to acquire [a share] in it, neither for others nor for himself:

Tosafot on Gittin 64b:1:1.hebrew: הני מילי לחומרא אבל לקולא לא - ואפי' לרב ששת דאמר בפרק בכל מערבין (עירובין דף לב.) דבשל תורה נמי חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו, הני מילי במקום שאם לא יעשה שליחותו יבא המשלח לידי עבירה אם יסמוך על השליח; אבל כאן, אם לא יתן גט או לא יקדש, שלא יבא המשלח לידי עבירה בשביל כך, מודה רב ששת דאין חזקה שליח עושה שליחותו לקולא. ושם הארכתי:
Tosafot on Gittin 64b:1:1.english: This matter [applies] to stringency, but to leniency, no - And even according to Rav Sheshet, who says in the chapter [entitled] BeKhol Me'arvin (Eruvin 32a) that even in biblical matters there is a presumption [that] an agent performs his agency — that applies [only] in a case where, if he does not perform his agency, the sender will come to [commit] a transgression if he relies on the agent. But here, if he does not deliver the bill of divorce or does not betroth [a woman], [such] that the sender will not come to [commit] a transgression on account of that, Rav Sheshet concedes that there is no presumption [that] an agent performs his agency for leniency. And there I elaborated:

Tosafot on Gittin 64b:4:1.hebrew: נערה המאורסה היא ואביה כו' - פירש בקונטרס: דוקא נערה, אבל קטנה — דוקא אביה ולא היא, אם יש לה אב; והא דאמר בגמרא "רבנן סברי יד יתירא זכי לה רחמנא", היינו יד עצמה שניתוסף לה כשהיא נערה, דכשהיתה קטנה לא היה לה יד כי אם יד אב. ושוב הגיה רש"י בפ"ב דקידושין (דף מג:) דה"ה קטנה, והא דנקט "נערה" — להודיעך כח דרבי יהודה, וכן עיקר. והביא ראיה רבינו יצחק ב"ר מאיר, דבפרק שני דקדושין (דף מד:) פריך לרב נחמן, דאמר "אין נערה עושה שליח לקבל גיטה מיד בעלה", מהא דתנן: "קטנה שאמרה התקבל לי גיטי — אינו גט עד שיגיע גט לידה; הא נערה — הרי זה גט", ומשני: כשאין לה אב. אבל מעיקרא סלקא דעתן דאיירי כשיש לה אב, ואפילו הכי קתני "עד שיגיע גט לידה", ש"מ דאף אם יש לה אב, אם הגיע גט לידה — מגורשת; והא דאמרי' בגמרא "יד יתירא זכי לה רחמנא", היינו יד האב, דיד עצמה עיקר שיש לה בבגרות, ולא ניתן לה יד האב לבטל כח ידה, ור' יהודה סבר דבטל כח ידה וניתן לה יד האב:
Tosafot on Gittin 64b:4:1.english: A betrothed young woman, she and her father, etc. - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: [This applies] specifically to a *na'arah* [young woman], whereas [for] a minor girl — specifically her father [receives her bill of divorce] and not she, if she has a father; and that which [the Gemara] says, "The Rabbis hold that the Merciful One granted her an additional hand," refers to her own hand that was added to her when she became a *na'arah*, for when she was a minor she had no hand [of her own], only [her] father's hand. And subsequently Rashi emended [his commentary] in the second chapter of Kiddushin (43b) [to say] that the same applies to a minor girl, and the reason [the Mishnah] stated "a *na'arah*" is to inform you of the extent of Rabbi Yehuda's [view]; and so is the primary [view]. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak bar Meir brought a proof [for this], for in the second chapter of Kiddushin (44b) [the Gemara] raises an objection against Rav Nachman, who said, "A *na'arah* cannot appoint an agent to receive her bill of divorce from her husband's hand," from that which we learned in a Mishnah: "A minor girl who said, 'Receive my bill of divorce for me' — it is not a [valid] bill of divorce until the bill of divorce reaches her hand; [implying that] a *na'arah*, by contrast — it is a [valid] bill of divorce." And [the Gemara] answers: [That Mishnah is referring to] when she has no father. However, initially it occurred to us that [the Mishnah] is dealing with [a case] where she has a father, and even so it teaches "until the bill of divorce reaches her hand." Learn from this that even if she has a father, if the bill of divorce reaches her hand, she is divorced; and that which we say in the Gemara, "The Merciful One granted her an additional hand," refers to the father's hand, for her own hand is the primary one, which she has upon reaching adulthood, and the father's hand was not given to her to nullify the power of her [own] hand; whereas Rabbi Yehuda holds that the power of her [own] hand is nullified and the father's hand is given to her:

Tosafot on Gittin 64b:4:2.hebrew: וכל שאינה יכולה לשמור את גיטה כו' - פי' בקונטרס: אפילו על ידי אביה, דהא שוטה היא, וא"ר יצחק: "ושלחה מביתו" — מי שמשלחה ואינה חוזרת; וכן בפרק חרש (יבמות דף קיג:). ור"ת מפרש דעל ידי אביה מתגרשת, אע"ג שאינה יודעת לשמור את גיטה, והורה כך הלכה למעשה. דהא לר' ינאי, דדריש התם מ"ונתן בידה" — מי שיש לה יד לגרש את עצמה, יצתה זו כו', לפי אותו טעם מגורשת על ידי אביה, דהא אפילו פיקחת אביה מקבל את גיטה. ותנא דבי ר' ישמעאל, דמפיק מ"ושלחה", לא פליג עליה אלא בהא דמפיק מקרא אחרינא, אבל משמע דליכא בינייהו מידי. וטעמא: כיון שיש לה אב, הוא שומרה מלחזור. ועוד, דבירושלמי בהדיא קורא אותה שיש לה אב "יכולה לשמור את גיטה". א"כ, מתגרשת על ידי אביה לכולי עלמא, דהא לא מצרכי הכא אלא שתהא יכולה לשמור את גיטה. וכן נראה, דאי כשאינה יכולה לשמור את גיטה אינה מתגרשת אפי' ע"י אביה, א"כ לענין קדושין נמי לא תתקדש, ד"ויצאה והיתה" כתיב, דאיתקש הויה ליציאה. ולפי זה לא מיתוקמא הך סיפא ד"כל שאינה יודעת כו'" ביש לה אב כר"י, אלא כרבנן; דלר"י, מאי איריא אינה יודעת לשמור את גיטה דאינה מתגרשת על ידי עצמה? אפילו יודעת לשמור אינה מתגרשת על ידי עצמה! אבל באין לה אב, מיתוקמא שפיר כרבי יהודה:
Tosafot on Gittin 64b:4:2.english: And anyone who is unable to safeguard her bill of divorce, etc. - Rashi explained: Even through her father [she cannot be divorced], for she is mentally incompetent, and Rabbi Yitzchak said [regarding the verse] "and he sends her out of his house" — [this applies to] one whom he sends out and she does not return; and so too in the chapter [entitled] Cheresh (Yevamot 113b). And Rabbeinu Tam explains that through her father she can be divorced even though she does not know how to safeguard her bill of divorce, and he ruled thus in practice. For according to Rabbi Yannai, who derives there from "and he shall place [it] in her hand" — one who has a "hand" [i.e., legal capacity] to divorce herself, excluding this one, etc. — according to that reason, she is divorced through her father, for even [when she is] mentally competent her father receives her bill of divorce! And the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, who derives [the exclusion] from "and he sends her out," does not disagree with him except in that he derives it from a different verse, but it implies that there is no practical difference between them. And the reason is that since she has a father, he guards her from returning. And furthermore, in the Yerushalmi it explicitly calls one who has a father "able to safeguard her bill of divorce"; if so, she is divorced through her father according to everyone, for here they only require that she be able to safeguard her bill of divorce. And so it appears [correct], for if when she cannot safeguard her bill of divorce she cannot be divorced even through her father, then with respect to betrothal too she could not be betrothed, for it is written "and she goes out... and she becomes [another man's]," where "becoming" [betrothal] is compared to "going out" [divorce]. And according to this [interpretation], this latter clause, "Anyone who does not know, etc.," cannot be established as referring to one who has a father according to Rabbi Yehuda, but rather according to the Rabbis; for according to Rabbi Yehuda, why specify "one who does not know how to safeguard her bill of divorce" as unable to be divorced on her own? Even one who does know how to safeguard [it] cannot be divorced on her own! However, regarding one who has no father, it is well established [even] according to Rabbi Yehuda:

Tosafot on Gittin 64b:8:1.hebrew: כל שמבחנת בין גיטה לדבר אחר - היינו כפעוטות, ופעוטות היינו כבר שית וכבר עשר, כל חד לפום חורפיה, כדאמרי' לקמן, וכנגדן בקטנה מתגרשת. והשתא, אי שיעורא דרב יהודה דאמר "חפץ ומחזירו לאחר שעה" קודם לשיעורא דפעוטות, היה סברת רב יהודה אפכא לגמרי מדרב חסדא; דלרב יהודה זוכה לאחרים קודם שיהא מקחו מקח וממכרו ממכר, ולרב חסדא הוה אפכא, דפעוטות מקחן מקח וממכרן ממכר, ואינן זוכים לאחרים עד שיביאו שתי שערות לרב חסדא, מדפריך עליה משפחה שלא הביאה שתי שערות:
Tosafot on Gittin 64b:8:1.english: Any [girl] who distinguishes between her bill of divorce and something else - This is like [the level of] pe'utot [young children of the age of discernment], and pe'utot means like a six-year-old or like a ten-year-old, each one according to his sharpness, as we say below, and correspondingly in [the case of] a minor girl, she can be divorced. And now, if the measure of Rav Yehudah, who says "[one who is given] an object and returns it after a while," is earlier than the measure of pe'utot, [then] Rav Yehudah's reasoning would be completely opposite to that of Rav Ḥisda; for according to Rav Yehudah, [a minor] can acquire on behalf of others before his purchase is a [valid] purchase and his sale is a [valid] sale, whereas according to Rav Ḥisda it is the opposite, for [with] pe'utot, their purchase is a [valid] purchase and their sale is a [valid] sale, yet they cannot acquire on behalf of others until they grow two [pubic] hairs according to Rav Ḥisda, since [the Gemara] raises an objection against him from a maidservant who has not grown two [pubic] hairs:
